quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you turn. If you turn too fast, your motorcycle may drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: To flash your lights.
To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
To ensure that your motorcycle is painted a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on day and night to help others see you. Use your high beam whenever it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: If you will be carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely have to:

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure adjustments.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct tire pressure.

questions.question: When consumed together, the effects of alcohol and drugs:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is consumed alone.
Often balance out.
Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
questions.explanation: Drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can make it unsafe to ride. Mixing medications with alcohol can be especially dangerous.

questions.question: A motorcyclist may not place a toll road transponder:

options.text: On the windshield of their motorcycle.
In their pocket.
Under their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under their seat.
questions.explanation: You can place a transponder in your pocket, in a cycle net on the gas tank, on a license plate device, in a storage compartment, or on the windshield. You cannot place it under your seat.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists are:

options.text: Sneakers.
Sturdy boots.
Sandals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Wear leather boots that are high and sturdy. They protect your feet and support your ankles.

questions.question: If traveling with a load, the load should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible. Placing a load on a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: With the front brake only
With the rear brake only
With both brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: With both brakes
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually maintain control as long as the motorcycle stays upright and straight.

questions.question: There may be less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is leaning.
A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do so carefully.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Also downshift.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Help you see others and help others see you.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Let other drivers share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and help others see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and helps them see you. It also helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist NOT do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Get ready to use the clutch and brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position where other drivers can see you. Get your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to react quickly. Slow down when approaching an intersection. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers about what you plan to do.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake, then press it again gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then press it again gently.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure right away. Then apply the brake again with gentle, steady pressure.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately—not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign has white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Fit into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly to your actions. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. When carrying a passenger, reduce your speed, begin slowing earlier when you need to stop, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: What is a benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft more easily off other vehicles.
You can stop more quickly.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Always keep space around your motorcycle. If a hazard appears, you will have more time to respond and more room to move safely.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It connects to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that connect the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Wearing what can help you avoid serious injury in a crash?

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury while riding a motorcycle. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see better.
Keep riding at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. It is harder to see at night, so you need extra time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects you from pebbles thrown by other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: When bright sunlight makes turn signals hard to see, a rider should:

options.text: Continue using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk their horn to tell other drivers about upcoming turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard for other drivers to see. It is important to clearly communicate with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Stay away from the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to the left or right side and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:

options.text: Has no cracks or defects.
Looks nice.
Fits loosely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you are involved in a crash that causes more than $1,000 in property damage, you must:

options.text: File a report only if you plan to report it to your insurance company.
Submit a report to the DMV.
Contact the highway department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Submit a report to the DMV.
questions.explanation: If you are involved in a crash with property damage over $1,000, you must submit a report to the DMV. The DMV can take action if you were involved in an uninsured crash that you must report.

questions.question: To avoid getting too tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine can make fatigue worse because you will become very tired when it wears off. Wind, rain, snow, and other weather can also increase fatigue, so dress warmly and consider getting a windshield if you ride long distances.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally:

options.text: Ride in a single line.
Pair up.
Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is generally best for a group of riders. It keeps the group close together while giving each rider enough space cushion. Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right if:

options.text: There is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
They ride on the road shoulder.
They ride on level grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.
